newsitem.title: FRANCE: Parcel bomb sent to French Jewish newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Parcel bomb sent to French Jewish newspaper.

text.p: The editor-in-chief of France's Jewish newspaper, Tribune Juive, said on Wednesday he had narrowly escaped death when he opened a booby-trapped package addressed to him.
Editor Yves Derai said he thought the parcel contained a video cassette when it arrived on Tuesday.

"It was a device with a container filled with chlorate and a rudimentary detonator. Strangely enough I was unable to get the tape out of the envelope so I tore the package open. That's why I didn't trigger the detonator," he said.

Derai quoted police investigators as saying there was no apparent link with the bombing of a regional express train at Port Royal station in Paris on Tuesday which killed two people and bore the hallmarks of Algerian Moslem fundamentalists.
"But the police do not rule out a link because last year during bombings (in France by suspected Algerian Moslem fundamentalists) one of the targets was a Jewish school," Derai said.
On September 7, 1995, a car bomb injured 14 people outside a Jewish school in the Lyon suburb of Villeurbanne. The bomb went off minutes before students left for the day.
